answer: Rate-limit identities by shared compute: each new agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle tied to its own key that takes about 40 minutes on 8 GB of RAM, and must redo it every 30 days. One honest bot barely notices, but a farm wanting 1,000 fakes needs 8 TB of RAM booked before dawn. Like a lotus that rises only from its own roots, every identity carries its own cost, and a plume of cheap clones simply never gets past the first gate.
